sentences.text:
The petitioner in M.V.C.No.5577/2024 &
M.V.C.No.5578/2024 have filed these claim petitions
under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking
compensation for the injuries sustained by them in a
road traffic accident.
 Scch-24 3 Mvc 5577/2024
 C/w
 Mvc 5578/2024
 2.

These two petitions have arisen out of the same
accident.

Therefore as per Clubbing memo dated 21-03-
2025 filed by the counsel for Petitioners, these two
petitions have been clubbed together for common
evidence and common disposal.

3. The case of the petitioners is as follows:-
 That on 13-03-2024 at about 10-30 p.m.,
petitioner Mohan Kumar.H in M.V.C. No.5577/2024
was riding motorcycle bearing No.KA-52-W-5904 along
with petitioner Manjunatha G V in Mvc No.5578/2024
as a pillion rider and when they were proceeding on
Tubagunte village gate, Doddabelavangala Hobli,
Doddaballapura Taluk, Bangalore Rural District, at that
time the driver of Borewell Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-05-
Ae-9531 came in a rash and negligent manner and
dashed against the petitioners motorcycle, result of
which the petitioners in both the cases fell down and
sustained grievous injuries.
Mohan Kumar H vs Ramaswamy A on 6 October, 2025
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146000876/
2

 4.

Immediately after the accident, the
petitioners in both the cases were shifted to Govt.
Hospital Doddaballapura, wherein first aid treatment
was given and then they were shifted to Nimhans
Hospital, Bangalore, wherein admitted as an inpatient
 Scch-24 4 Mvc 5577/2024
 C/w
 Mvc 5578/2024
for about 5 days respectively.

So far, the petitioners
incurred Rs.80,000/- towards medical expenses and
other incidental charges etc.,
 5.

Prior to the accident, the petitioner in Mvc.
No. 5577/2024 was hale and healthy.

He was doing
coolie and agriculture work and earning sum of
Rs.25,000/- per month.

Due to the permanent
disability suffered on account of the grievous injuries he
is not in a position to do the work as earlier.

He has
suffered mental pain and agony.

6. Prior to the accident, the petitioner in
MVC.No.5578/2024 was hale and healthy.

He was
doing collie and agriculture work and earning sum of
Rs.25,000/- per month.

Due to the permanent
disability suffered on account of the grievous injuries he
is not in a position to do the work as earlier.

He has
suffered mental pain and agony.

7. In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.1
- the R.C. owner of Borewell Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-
05-Ae-9531 has remained absent.

Hence he was placed
exparte.
 Scch-24 5 Mvc 5577/2024
 C/w
 Mvc 5578/2024
 8.

Respondent no.2/ the insurer of Borewell
Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-05-AE-9531 in both the cases
has filed written statement and admitted the coverage
of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to the
terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.

The
respondent

no.2 has contended that the accident in
question has occurred due to the negligence on the part
of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-52-W-5904
Mohan Kumar H vs Ramaswamy A on 6 October, 2025
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146000876/
3

who rode the said motorcycle in a rash and negligent
manner and without observing the traffic rules on the
road has came in contact with the alleged insured
vehicle on service road from opposite direction and that
the driver of the insured vehicle was not holding valid
and effective driving license.

9. On the basis of the above pleadings the
following issues are framed:
 I S S U E S in Mvc 5577/2024
 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that, he
 has sustained injuries on account of road
 traffic accident on 13-03-2024 at about 10-30
 pm., on Tubagunte Village Gate,
 Doddabelavangala Hobli, Doddaballapura
 Taluk, Bangalore Rural District, due to rash
 and negligent driving of the driver of Borewell
 Lorry bearing No.KA-05-AE-9531?

2. Whether petitioner is entitled for
 compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?
from whom?
3. What order or award?

I S S U E S in Mvc No.5578/2024
 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that, he has
 sustained injuries on account of road traffic
 accident on 13-03-2024 at about 10-30 pm., on
 Tubagunte Village Gate, Doddabelavangala
 Hobli, Doddaballapura Taluk, Bangalore Rural
 District, due to rash and negligent driving of the
 driver of Borewell Lorry bearing No.KA-05-AE-
 9531?

2. Whether petitioner is entitled for
 compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?
from whom?
3. What order or award?

10. The petitioner in M.V.C.No.5577/2024 got
examined himself as Pw1 and got marked documents
as Ex.P1 to Ex.P9 and Ex.P14.

The petitioner in
M.V.C.No.5578/2024 got examined himself as Pw.2 and
got marked Exs.P10 to Ex.P13.

They have also
examined Medical Record Officer as Pw.3 and got

4

marked Ex.15 to 20.

The respondent no.2 has not
adduced evidence on its behalf.

Heard the arguments of learned counsel for
petitioners and learned counsel for respondent no.2.
 12.

My findings on the above issues in
M.V.C.No.5577/2024 are as follows:-
 Issue No.1- In the Affirmative
 Issue No.2- Partly in the affirmative
 Issue No.3- As per final Order.

for the following :
 13.

My findings on the above issues in
M.V.C.No.5578/2024 are as follows:-
 Issue No.1- In the Affirmative
 Issue No.2- Partly in the affirmative
 Issue No.3- As per final Order

 for the following :
Reasons

14 . Issue No.1 and 2 in M.V.C.No.5577/2024
and M.V.C.No.5578/2024:- As these issues are
interconnected they are taken up together for common
discussion to avoid repetition of facts.

15 . In order to substantiate the contention, the
petitioner in Mvc No.5577/2024 is examined as Pw.1
and Petitioner in Mvc No.5578/2024 is examined as
Pw.2.

The PWs.1 and 2 have specifically deposed in
 Scch-24 8 Mvc 5577/2024
 C/w
 Mvc 5578/2024
their chief examination that the driver of Borewell Lorry
bearing No.KA-05-AE-9531 (here in after called the
offending vehicle) came in a rash and negligent manner
and dashed against the petitioners motorcycle and
caused for the accident, result of which the petitioners
in both the cases sustained grievous injuries.

Mohan Kumar H vs Ramaswamy A on 6 October, 2025
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146000876/
5

 16.

In support of the claim and to prove the rash
and negligent driving of the offending vehicle, the P.W.1
and Pw.2 have relied upon Ex.P1 to P6 which are the
police records such as F.I.R with Complaint, wound
certificate, spot mahazar, notice u/Sec. 133 Imv Act
and reply given there to, Imv report, charge sheet, etc.,
 17.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by
Hanumantharaju G, case has been registered against
the driver of offending vehicle in Crime No.0041/2024
of Doddabelavangala Police Station for the offence
punishable under sections 279, 337 of Ipc.

The
Investigation officer after investigation filed charge
sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the
offence punishable under sections 279, 337, 338 of Ipc.
 18.

The learned counsel for Respondent No.2
during the course of argument has vehemently
 Scch-24 9 Mvc 5577/2024
 C/w
 Mvc 5578/2024
submitted about the delay in lodging the complaint and
submitted that though the offending vehicle was not
involved in the accident and though accident in
question was not occurred due to the rash and
negligent driving of the offending vehicle, but the
complainant in collision with the owner of the offending
vehicle has falsely implicated the offending vehicle in
order to get the compensation and that the spot of
accident is in the middle of the road, hence petitioner
too has contributed negligency.

By referring the Ex.P.14
it was further argued that, at the time of accident
petitioner was not wearing helmet and both of them
were under influence of alcohol hence, they are not
entitled for compensation.

19. In the light of the contention taken by the
respondent no.2, if Ex.P14 is perused it is true that, in
the Ex.P14, it is mentioned that, Mohan Kumar i.e.,
petitioner in Mvc No. 5577/2024 was under the
influence of alcohol.

But there is no any
evidence/report as to the quantity of alcohol consumed
by the petitioner.

30 Ml is the permissible limit and if
any person consuming 30 ml of alcohol drives the
vehicle then it will not attract any offence.

Further, the
respondent no.2 cannot take the said defence for
 Scch-24 10 Mvc 5577/2024
Mohan Kumar H vs Ramaswamy A on 6 October, 2025

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146000876/
6

 C/w
 Mvc 5578/2024
exonerating them from paying the compensation.

No
charge sheet has been filed against the petitioner in
Mvc No.5577/2024 alleging of his riding the motor
cycle under the influence of alcohol or that both the
petitioners were traveling without head gear.

If really
the petitioners were traveling in the motor cycle without
wearing head gear or under the influence of alcohol
then the penal provision would attract and that itself
would not be a ground to say
that the petitioners have
also contributed negligence

. So far as the delay in lodging the complaint is
concerned, it is true that, though the accident in
question has occurred on 13.03.2024 but complaint
came to be lodged on 15.03.2024 and there is delay of 2
days in lodging the complaint.

In the complaint and in
the Fir reason for delay has been explained stating
that, the father of the petitioner in Mvc No.5577/2024
who is the complainant was engaged in providing
medical treatment to the injured.

Though the complaint
was lodged after 2 days of the accident but if the
medical records are perused, soon after the accident the
petitioners have taken treatment on the history of the
road traffic accident.

Hence, when delay has been
properly explained, the delay in lodging the complaint
 Scch-24 11 Mvc 5577/2024
 C/w
 Mvc 5578/2024
would not go to the root of the case of the petitioners.

If
spot mahazer is perused, at the time of accident, the
petitioners were proceeding from Kathi Hosahalli
towards Hulikunte in a service road and the offending
vehicle which came from opposite direction i.e., from
Hulikante towards Katti Hosahalli dashed against the
motor cycle of the petitioners. It is true that, the
accident in question has occurred some where in the
middle of the road but not exactly on the middle of the
road.

As per the spot mahazar and the photographs of
the scene of occurrence, there is white line in the
middle of the road so also on both sides of the road.

The
offending vehicle by crossing the middle line came
towards Kathi Hosahalli - Hulikunte Road and hit to
the motor cycle of the petitioners.

Had the offending
vehicle not crossed the middle line, this accident would
Mohan Kumar H vs Ramaswamy A on 6 October, 2025
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146000876/
7

not have occurred.

sentences.text:
Though, the respondent no.2 has
taken the contention that, petitioners too have
contributed negligence but they have not examined the
driver of the offending vehicle or any of the eye witness
to substantiate their contention.

Hence, the materials
placed on record clearly reveals the rash and negligent
act on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

Hence, issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative in
both the cases.
Issue No.2 in M.V.C.No.5577/2024:-

P.W.1 has given evidence to the effect of his
sustained severe injuries.

He has produced wound
certificate at Ex.P.2.

As per the wound certificate,
petitioner has sustained two injuries which are simple
in nature.

The petitioner sustained cut lacerated wound
over the scalp and Multiple abrasion over the body.

It
was vehemently argued by the learned counsel for
petitioner that even though in the wound certificate the
nature of injury is mentioned as simple injury but
petitioner has taken treatment for 5 days as an
inpatient and he has incurred medical expenses to the
tune of Rs.47,434/- hence, petitioner has sustained
grievous injuries.

22. As observed supra, the wound certificate
issued from the hospital where the petitioner has taken
treatment discloses that, petitioner has sustained
simple injuries.

The petitioner has not examined the
medical officer who has issued wound certificate to say
that the injuries sustained by him are grievous in
nature and that in the wound certificate it is wrongly
mentioned as simple in nature. When there is no contra
evidence against the wound certificate at Ex.P2 and
when petitioner himself has produced Ex.P2, under
 Scch-24 13 Mvc 5577/2024
 C/w
 Mvc 5578/2024
such circumstances there is every reason to believe that
petitioner has sustained only simple injuries.
 23.

Mr.Kiran Bharadwaj-Medical Record Officer at

8

Siddarath Hospital, Nelamangala, Bangalore Rural
District is examined as Pw.3 and through him Mlc,
Discharge summary, Scan report, x-ray film and case
sheet are marked as Ex.P16 to Ex.

The Discharge summary as per Ex.P17 issued
from Siddartha Hospital, Nelamangala discloses that
petitioner has taken treatment from 15-03-2024 to 19-
03-2024.

Thus the petitioner has taken treatment as
inpatient for a period of 4 days.

The petitioner has not
examined the medical officer who has given treatment to
him and there is no evidence on record to say that
petitioner
has suffered permanent disability

. As such
there is no loss of future income.

Hence, petitioner is
not entitled for compensation under the head of loss of
future income.

25. Towards pain and sufferings, the petitioner
shown to have sustained two simple injuries.

Hence
taking into consideration the nature of injuries
sustained by the petitioner, time taken for treatment
 Scch-24 14 Mvc 5577/2024
 C/w
 Mvc 5578/2024
and sufferings during the treatment etc, it is reasonable
to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of
Rs.40,000/- towards pain and suffering.

26. So far as the medical expenses incurred by the
petitioner are concerned, he has produced 21 medical
bills for Rs.47,434/- as per Ex.P8.

Hence, petitioner is
entitled for compensation under the head medical
expenses to the tune of Rs.47,434/-.

27. It is stated that petitioner was aged about 22
years.

He was working as Collie and also Agriculturist
and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m..

But to substantiate the
said contention petitioner has not produced any
materials.

Hence this court considering the age of
petitioner, year of accident and place of residence of the
petitioner, taken the income of the petitioner at
Rs.16,500/- p.m.
 28.

The petitioner has sustained simple injuries
and has taken treatment for 4 days as inpatient at
Siddarath Hospital, Nelamangala, Bangalore Rural
Mohan Kumar H vs Ramaswamy A on 6 October, 2025

District.
Hence the nature of injuries sustained by the

petitioner, which are simple in nature it is reasonable to
hold that period of one month as complete laid down
 Scch-24 15 Mvc 5577/2024
 C/w
 Mvc 5578/2024
period.

Hence taking into consideration the avocation of
petitioner and loss of income caused from the said
avocation, this court takes the loss of income during
laid down period as Rs.16,500/- p.m. for one month.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for a sum of
Rs.16,500/- towards loss of income during the laid
down period .
 29.

From the evidence of Pw1 and as borne out
by medical records, petitioner has taken treatment as
inpatient at Siddarath Hospital, Nelamangala,
Bangalore Rural District.

Further for taking treatment
as inpatient in the said hospital he was traveled to
hospital for treatment.

He has taken nourishment and
needs further nourishment at this age and incurred
other incidental expenses.

Therefore all together
incidental expenses is assessed at Rs 15,000/- taking
in to consideration the cost of living and value of the
money during the year 2024.
 30.

The petitioner at his age of 22 years has
suffered simple injuries which definitely would cause
some amount of discomfort and loss of amenities in life.

Hence, petitioner is entitled for compensation under the
head loss of amenities and discomfort to the tune of
 Scch-24 16 Mvc 5577/2024
 C/w

Rs.50,000/-.

Thus the Petitioner is entitled for
compensation under the following heads:

 No.

 charges and nourishing food
 & other incidental charges

Therefore this court holds that petitioner is entitled for
Rs.1,68,934/- (Rupees One Lakh Sixty Eight Thousand Nine
Hundred Thirty Four only).
 31. Issue No.2 in M.V.C.No.5578/2024:-
 P.W.2 has given evidence to the effect of his
sustained severe injuries.

He has produced wound
certificate at Ex.P.10.

As per the wound certificate, the
petitioner has sustained two injuries of which injury
no.1 is grievous in nature and injury no.2 is simple in
nature.

The petitioner has stated that he took treatment
as an inpatient at Siddartha Hospital, Nelamangala for
4 days.

But he has not produced discharge summary to
 Scch-24 17 Mvc 5577/2024
 C/w
 Mvc 5578/2024
evidence that he has taken treatment for nearly 4 days
as an inpatient.
32 . It is submitted by the petitioner that he was
working

as collie and also agriculturist and earning
sum of Rs.25,000/- per month and

due to the accident
it could not possible for him to do the said work and
that on account of the injuries sustained by him he is
getting pain every now and then which incapacitated
him from doing the work as before the accident.

33. Now coming to the aspect of quantifying the
compensation on different heads, the petitioner has
suffered one grievous injury which made him to suffer
pain and agony.

The petitioner has stated that he has
spend Rs.80,000/- towards his treatment, but not
produced any medical documents.

The petitioner has
not examined the Medical officer to prove that he has
suffered any disability so as to get compensation under
the head loss of future income.

The petitioner even has
not produced case sheet.

Hence having regard to the
pain and agony endured and loss of comforts and
amenities on account of sustaining such injuries and
incidental expenses incurred by the petitioner, this
 Scch-24 18 Mvc 5577/2024

Tribunal inclines to award global compensation of
Rs.90,000/-.
 34.

As regarding liability is concerned, there is no
dispute that offending vehicle was insured with 2 nd
respondent and policy was in force as on the date of
accident.

Further the driver of the offending vehicle
had driving license to drive the offending vehicle as on
the date of accident.

Hence it can be said that all the
documents pertaining to the vehicle in question was
valid and in force as on the date of accident.

Hence by
fastening liability on the respondent no.2 this court
directs the respondent no.2 to pay compensation to the
petitioner along with interest at 6% per annum from
the date of accident till the date of payment of entire
amount.
Accordingly Issue No. 2 is answered.

35. Issue No.3 in Mvc No.5577/2024 and
M.V.C.No.5578/2024 :- In the light of findings given on
Issue No.1 and 2 in Mvc No.5577/2024 and Mvc
